1.c4 e6 2.Nf3.strategy: Develops the king's knight, guards d4 and e5 and commits no pawn. White keeps every set-up open, from a Queen's Gambit structure to a kingside fianchetto, and Black still has to decide how to meet the c4-pawn. Flexible and safe, with the usual character of the English: a slow, manoeuvring game.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3.strategy: Develops the queen's knight, adds control of d5 and e4 and keeps the d-, e- and g-pawns free for later. It prepares to answer ...d5 by building a centre or by exchanging, while ...Bb4 can pin it and double White's pawns. Flexible, with fewer commitments than 2.d4.

1.c4 e6 2.d4.strategy: Occupies the centre at once: the d4-pawn controls c5 and e5 and, with the c4-pawn, bears on d5. White gives up the English flexibility for a Queen's Gambit type of game with the first claim on space. Black can allow it with ...d5 or fight it with an Indian set-up.

1.c4 e6 2.g3.strategy: Prepares Bg2, which presses on d5 and b7 along the long diagonal, and keeps the knights flexible. The cost is time: the c4-pawn has no defender yet, so 2...d5 attacks it at once and Black takes the centre. A patient, positional choice.

1.c4 e6 2.e4.strategy: Takes the centre with the c- and e-pawns and transposes to a French Defence in which White has played c4 instead of d4. After 2...d5 Black attacks both pawns, and White is left with an isolated d-pawn if the centre is exchanged. Sound, but it gives up the English character of the opening.

1.c4 e6 2.b3.strategy: Prepares Bb2 on the long diagonal toward g7 and protects the c4-pawn against ...d5. White builds a flexible set-up, but Black develops freely and takes the centre. Sound, but slower than developing a knight.

1.c4 e6 2.d3.strategy: Protects the c4-pawn, supports a later e4 and frees the c1-bishop. The d3-pawn is modest, though: it takes no part in the fight for d5 or d4, and Black takes space in the centre. Sound, but more passive than 2.d4.

1.c4 e6 2.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop's diagonal, which also guards c4, and prepares a compact set-up in the centre. It shuts in the c1-bishop, and after 2...d5 3.cxd5 exd5 Black's c8-bishop is free and the game is easy for Black. Sound but passive.

1.c4 e6 2.a3.strategy: Stops ...Bb4 and prepares b4, but it develops nothing and spends a tempo. Black takes the centre at once while White's pieces are still at home.

1.c4 e6 2.a4.strategy: Gains a little queenside space but leaves b4 as a permanent hole, since neither the a- nor the c-pawn can guard it any more. It develops nothing, and Black takes the centre at once.

1.c4 e6 2.f4.strategy: Takes e5 but develops no piece and opens the e1-h4 diagonal, so 2...Qh4+ forces 3.g3 at once. White's kingside is loosened before any piece is out, and Black continues freely.

1.c4 e6 2.g4.strategy: Gains kingside space but leaves the pawn loose: 2...Qh4 attacks it at once and pins the f2-pawn, so White must spend another move to keep it. The kingside is loosened before a single piece has developed.

1.c4 e6 2.h3.strategy: A waiting move: it neither fights for the centre nor develops a piece. Black develops with a free hand.

1.c4 e6 2.h4.strategy: A flank thrust that does nothing for the centre or development and loosens the kingside without a target. White has lost a tempo, and Black replies ...d5 with an easy game.

1.c4 e6 2.Na3.strategy: Guards c4 from the rim and heads for c2 or b5, but the knight stands far from the centre. Black can take the centre at once, or take with 2...Bxa3 3.bxa3, doubling and isolating White's a-pawns at the cost of the bishop pair.

1.c4 e6 2.Nh3.strategy: A rim knight heading for f4, which leaves the natural f3-square unused. After 2...d5 3.cxd5 exd5 the c8-bishop eyes h3, and ...Bxh3 gxh3 would leave White with doubled, isolated h-pawns.

1.c4 e6 2.Qc2.strategy: Guards c4 and supports e4, but brings the queen out before the minor pieces. Black takes the centre with ...d5 or gains time against the queen, and White has little to show for the early queen.

1.c4 e6 2.Qb3.strategy: Eyes b7, which the c8-bishop already guards, so there is no threat. Black develops or takes space with ...d5, while the early queen has no good follow-up.

1.c4 e6 2.Qa4.strategy: Brings the queen out to the a4-e8 diagonal, where it threatens nothing because d7 is guarded. Black simply develops, with the queen offside on a4.

1.c4 e6 2.b4.strategy: Leaves the pawn undefended on the open f8-a3 diagonal, and 2...Bxb4 wins it at once. White gets only the half-open b-file and an easy development of the c1-bishop in return.

1.c4 e6 2.f3.strategy: Opens the e1-h4 diagonal and loses a pawn: 2...Qh4+ forces 3.g3, since the king cannot go to f2, and 3...Qxc4 takes the undefended c-pawn. The move also takes f3 from the g1-knight.

1.c4 e6 2.c5.strategy: Gains space but leaves the pawn undefended: 2...Bxc5 wins it at once, since ...e6 has opened the f8-bishop's diagonal. 3.d4 gains a tempo on the bishop, but White is simply a pawn down.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the kingside knight, controls e4 and commits Black to nothing in the centre yet. The e6-pawn keeps every set-up open, so Black can choose once White has shown its plan. The price is that Black has claimed no central space yet, and White can take it.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 d5.strategy: Claims the centre at once, with the e6-pawn as solid support, and heads for a closed, strategic fight over the centre. The cost is the c8-bishop, shut in behind the pawn chain until Black frees it.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 c5.strategy: Fights for d4 from the side and aims for a symmetrical structure in which Black is not short of space. The e6-pawn keeps ...d5 ready, but it blocks the c8-bishop for now, and after ...d5 an exchange on d5 and a later d4 can leave Black with an isolated d-pawn.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Nc6.strategy: Develops a piece and eyes d4 and e5, but the knight blocks the c-pawn and commits itself before Black's structure is clear. White can take the centre, while Black still has familiar set-ups. Sound, though less flexible than …Nf6 or …d5.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Be7.strategy: Develops the dark-squared bishop and clears the way for castling once the g8-knight is out, keeping the centre pawns for later. It gives up the active pin on the c3-knight and leaves White free to choose its set-up. Sound, but slower and less flexible than a developing move that fights for the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Bb4.strategy: Attacks the c3-knight and prepares …Bxc3 to double White's pawns. White can recapture on c3 without damage, or avoid the exchange and claim the bishop pair. Playable, but it commits the bishop before the centre is settled and is less direct than a move in the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 b6.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop on the long diagonal and to develop the kingside pieces. White can claim central space at once, so Black must be ready to hit the centre. Sound and flexible, but a less direct fight for the centre than occupying it.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 c6.strategy: Prepares …d5, usually with a solid pawn centre supported by c6 and e6 after d4. The move is slow and takes c6 from the b8-knight, and White can avoid that structure with e4, so that …d5 is met by exd5 and an early exchange of pawns. Sound, but less flexible than a direct central move.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 d6.strategy: Builds a compact pawn pair on d6 and e6 from which Black can develop and castle, with …e5 or …c5 as later breaks. It gives up the fight for the centre, and after d4 a hasty …e5 allows dxe5 dxe5 and an exchange of queens that costs Black the right to castle. Playable, though passive.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 f5.strategy: Takes e4 under control and aims for an aggressive kingside set-up, or a solid pawn wall on c6, d5, e6 and f5. It weakens e6 and the e8–h5 diagonal, and White meets it by taking the centre or fianchettoing the king's bishop. Sound enough, but committal and less solid than …d5.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 g6.strategy: Prepares …Bg7 to press along the long diagonal. The set-up is slow, and White can build the centre before Black has made a claim in it. Flexible, but slower than a direct central move.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Na6.strategy: Places the knight on the rim, where it eyes b4 and c5 but leaves d5 and the centre uncontested. White takes space while Black has lost time.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Qe7.strategy: Brings the queen out early, blocks the f8-bishop and leaves c7 without a defender, so Nb5 threatens Nxc7+ and wins time. White then builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Qf6.strategy: Brings the queen out early and takes f6 from the g8-knight. The queen's diagonal only reaches the c3-knight, which the b2- and d2-pawns cover, while Nb5 threatens Nxc7+ with a fork of king and rook and Ne4 attacks the queen, so Black loses more time.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Qg5.strategy: Puts the queen where d4 opens the c1-bishop's diagonal against it and Nf3 attacks it as well, so White develops with gain of time. The pressure on g2 is harmless, since Bf1 covers it.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Qh4.strategy: Eyes f2, which the king covers, and the c4-pawn, which nothing defends yet. White covers it with e3, opening the f1-bishop's diagonal, or with b3, and then gains time against the queen with Nf3 or g3 while Black has developed nothing.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Bd6.strategy: Blocks the d7-pawn, so …d5 is impossible while the bishop stays on d6, and invites Nb5, when Nxd6+ cxd6 would take the bishop pair and leave Black with doubled d-pawns. White then builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Bc5.strategy: Puts the bishop where d4 attacks it, so White gains central space with a tempo while Black retreats to b4 or e7.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Nh6.strategy: Puts the knight on the rim. After d4 the c1-bishop attacks it, and Bxh6 gxh6 would double the h-pawns, while …Nf5 can be met by e4 with a gain of time.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Ne7.strategy: Blocks the f8-bishop, whose only open diagonal runs through e7, and passes up the natural …Nf6. The knight supports …d5, but White takes the centre with e4 and d4 while Black untangles the kingside.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 a6.strategy: Spends a tempo on a flank pawn that neither fights for the centre nor develops a piece; it prepares …b5 at best, which c4 already restrains. White builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 a5.strategy: Advances the a-pawn without purpose: it controls b4 but gives up …a6 against a knight on b5, and does nothing for the centre or development. White builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 f6.strategy: Weakens e6 and the e8–h5 diagonal and takes f6 from the g8-knight, with no development in return. White builds a broad centre at leisure, and the weakened diagonal invites Qh5+ once e4 is played.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 g5.strategy: Lunges on the kingside with nothing developed and weakens f6, h6 and the dark squares around the king for good. The d8-queen guards the pawn for now, but d4 opens the c1-bishop against it and h4 hits it again.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 h6.strategy: Prevents Bg5, but nothing threatens g5 yet, and the move does nothing for the centre or development. White builds the centre undisturbed.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 h5.strategy: Advances the rook pawn without purpose and weakens g5, since the h-pawn can no longer cover it from h6. It develops nothing and does nothing for the centre, so White simply builds the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 e5.strategy: Plays the e-pawn twice to reach the square that 1…e5 reached in one move, so White is a full tempo up in a Reversed Sicilian structure.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Ke7.strategy: Gives up castling for good and blocks the f8-bishop, with nothing gained in return. The king stays in the centre, where it becomes a target once White opens lines in the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 Ba3.strategy: Gives the bishop away: bxa3 takes it, and Black gets nothing in return.

1.c4 e6 2.Nc3 b5.strategy: Hangs a pawn: cxb5 wins it, and Black has neither development nor open lines to show for it.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 d5.strategy: Claims the centre at once with a pawn that the e6-pawn supports, much as in the French Defence. Black challenges White's c-pawn and fights for the middle from the start, and White's fianchetto bishop soon bears down on the d5 pawn. The cost is the c8-bishop, which stays shut in behind e6 until Black finds it a diagonal.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight and keeps every central plan open, a pawn on d5 or on c5, while preparing a solid set-up with the bishop on e7 and early castling. The price of staying flexible is that White chooses the pawn structure first.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 c5.strategy: Mirrors White's c-pawn and takes control of d4, so White cannot easily build a pawn centre there. With e6 already backing d5, Black keeps ...d5 and the development of both knights in reserve. The game becomes a symmetrical English structure: slow, manoeuvring and decided by piece play rather than by early pawn breaks.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 f5.strategy: Takes control of e4 and heads for a Dutch set-up, with the option of a Stonewall pawn wall. Black stakes a claim to the kingside and the initiative there, but the advance loosens the e8-h5 diagonal, and in the Stonewall the e5 square becomes a lasting hole. A sharper, more committal game than the other replies.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Nc6.strategy: Develops the knight and controls d4 and e5. The knight blocks the c-pawn, so ...c5 is ruled out for now, and White's g2-bishop will bear down on it. Sound, but Black commits a piece before the pawn structure is settled.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Be7.strategy: Develops the bishop and clears f8 for castling once the g8-knight is out. It claims no central space yet, so White can build a full centre without hindrance. Sound, but it leaves the choice of pawn structure to White.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 b6.strategy: Prepares ...Bb7 to fianchetto the queen's bishop, but a g2-bishop would look straight down the long diagonal at the a8-rook. Playing ...Bb7 at once loses the bishop to Bxb7, so Black first has to close or guard the diagonal. Playable, yet White gains time.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 c6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 behind a compact chain of pawns on c6, d5 and e6, and blocks the long diagonal of a future g2-bishop. The c8-bishop stays shut in behind e6, and White can take space at once. Sound, but slower than playing ...d5 immediately.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 d6.strategy: Prepares a compact set-up with the knight on f6, the bishop on e7 and castling, or a later ...e5. It concedes central space, so White builds a strong centre at leisure. Sound, though passive.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 g6.strategy: Prepares a fianchetto of Black's own, with the bishop on g7 and short castling to follow. Black has no pawn in the centre yet, so White can take space there. Sound, though passive.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Na6.strategy: Places the knight on the rim, where it eyes b4 and c5 but does little in the centre. White develops and takes the centre with time to spare.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Qe7.strategy: Puts the queen in front of the f8-bishop, which has no other open diagonal, so Black's kingside development waits on another queen move. White develops and takes the centre in the meantime.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Qf6.strategy: Brings the queen out to f6, where it eyes b2, which the c1-bishop guards, and takes f6 from the g8-knight. White develops and can gain time against the exposed queen.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Qg5.strategy: Sends the queen to g5 to eye the d2-pawn, but 3.d4 opens the c1-bishop's diagonal and attacks the queen, so White takes the centre with tempo.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Bd6.strategy: Blocks the d-pawn, so ...d5 has to wait until the bishop moves again, and leaves the bishop a target for e4-e5. White develops and takes the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Bc5.strategy: Eyes f2 and the g1-a7 diagonal, but 3.d4 attacks the bishop, which must move again while White has taken the centre with tempo.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Bb4.strategy: Looks at d2, which is guarded four times, so there is no threat, and 3.a3 drives the bishop away. White gets a useful pawn move for the time Black spends on retreating.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Nh6.strategy: Heads for f5, but the knight stands on the rim in the meantime, and g4 can later drive it from f5. White develops and takes the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Ne7.strategy: Blocks the f8-bishop, whose natural square is e7, and puts the knight where it does less than on f6. White takes space while Black's kingside development lags.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 a6.strategy: Prepares ...b5, but once the bishop stands on g2, ...b5 opens the long diagonal to the a8-rook, so the move mostly costs a tempo. White simply develops and takes the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 a5.strategy: Controls b4 but develops nothing and takes no part in the centre, and the a-pawn can never again cover b5. White has a free hand in the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 b5.strategy: Gambits a pawn after 3.cxb5, hoping for ...Bb7 along the open long diagonal against the h1-rook. White meets that by developing a piece or blocking the diagonal and keeps the extra pawn, so Black has little to show for it.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 f6.strategy: Takes f6 from the g8-knight, opens the e8-h5 diagonal to the king and leaves e6 without the f-pawn's support, all without developing a piece. White gains time and takes the centre.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 g5.strategy: Loosens the king's cover and leaves f6 and h6, which the g-pawn guarded, without pawn protection, and develops nothing. White gains time with d4, when the c1-bishop attacks the pawn, and can open lines with h4.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 h6.strategy: Spends a tempo guarding g5, where no white piece can go yet, and neither develops a piece nor claims the centre. White develops and takes the centre at leisure.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 h5.strategy: Prepares ...h4 against g3, but spends a tempo on a flank advance that weakens g5 and the kingside and develops nothing. White can ignore it or play h4 to stop the idea for good.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 e5.strategy: Plays the e-pawn twice and reaches the usual pawn centre against White's fianchetto set-up, but with White to move, so Black is a full tempo down on the reversed Sicilian. The pawn centre is sound, but White develops with an extra move in hand.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Qh4.strategy: Walks the queen onto a square the g3-pawn attacks, so 3.gxh4 wins it for nothing.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Ke7.strategy: Gives up castling for good and blocks the f8-bishop and the queen's d8-h4 diagonal, with nothing gained in return. White develops and takes the centre while the king stays in the middle.

1.c4 e6 2.g3 Ba3.strategy: The bishop stands on a square attacked by the b2-pawn and the b1-knight, so 3.bxa3 or 3.Nxa3 wins it for nothing.
